title: fix(database): analyze PostgreSQL schemas after database port
body:
Fixes #183307. Thanks @etzelm for the detailed reproduction and planner observations.

Related: #183327.

## What Problem This Solves

Porting a store to PostgreSQL leaves copied data, and the later agent memory rebuild, without planner statistics until autovacuum catches up. PostgreSQL backup restore uses the same bulk-copy path and has the same gap.

## User Impact

Newly ported and restored stores have statistics before returning to their caller. Agent ports refresh them again after the memory manager finishes and closes. Statistics refresh failures produce warnings while preserving the verified data; autovacuum can finish the optimization later.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared bulk-copy owner now runs namespace-scoped `ANALYZE` after canonical verification and commit, in a separate transaction. Catalog discovery includes the destination's derived tables, identifiers are quoted, and unrelated namespaces are untouched. A 10-second statement timeout and 1-second lock timeout bound the work. Port reports expose success/table counts or a warning, including the post-rebuild result. PostgreSQL backup restore automatically uses the same helper through the materializer.

The existing worker owns SQL and the post-port offline owner retains custody through the memory refresh. No configuration, CLI options, dependencies, schemas, data verification, or steady-state autovacuum policy change. Simplification review retained one statistics helper for all bulk-copy callers; no parallel restore implementation was introduced.

## Evidence

- Regression with the original materializer behavior: a populated table returned `reltuples = -1` instead of `1` with autovacuum disabled. After the fix, the state-port test checks statistics immediately after port and after both exact and sanitized restore.
- Node command regression: real port custody, PostgreSQL writes, and worker transport, with a fixed memory-plugin service; statistics reflect the new memory chunk before the command returns. The selected regression passes in 16.6 seconds of test time (63.0 seconds wall, including source preparation).
- PostgreSQL helper tests pass on Node: a quoted table name, a second namespace left unanalyzed, restored connection timeouts, and an actual conflicting lock that becomes a warning in about 1 second while committed rows remain readable.
- Isolated live owner proof against local PostgreSQL 17, autovacuum disabled: `doctorDatabasePort({ family: 'agent', to: 'postgres' })` ported 500 cache rows and ran the real bundled memory runtime, rebuilding one chunk in 22.7 seconds. Both phases reported `analyzed` for 47 tables. Immediately afterward, `pg_class.reltuples` was `500` for `cache_entries` and `1` for `memory_index_chunks`; `pg_stat_user_tables.last_analyze` was set for both.
- Production and infra-test typechecks pass; touched-file Oxlint and oxfmt pass; line-cap ratchet passes for all 13 changed source files; Madge reports zero import cycles; `git diff --check` passes. Fresh isolated Codex review found no actionable P0–P2 findings.

Consumer validation ran all 34 runnable files selected by the owner-basename scan on Node 26.12.1 (the scan also matched a live-only subagent file through `report.workers`; it has no changed-owner import and the normal runner excludes it). The initial run reported 808 passed tests, 9 failed, and 4 skipped across those 34 files. Two bounded follow-ups are now green, leaving only the storage-permission limitations below:

- Mixed-family round trips previously opened backup workers per operation: the first state round trip timed out at 124.2 seconds and left the shared test fixture mid-port for later cases. The suite now uses the existing pooled database-worker fixture, retaining real native worker protocol and SQL. Its first state round trip passes in 68.8 seconds; all five mixed-family cases pass with the original timeout and assertions. No retries or larger timeouts were added.
- The refusal/resume consumer now distinguishes stable descriptor/data verification from the new per-attempt statistics report. Reusing a verified anchor performs no new copy or ANALYZE; all original canonical-data and anchor-byte assertions remain. This case passes in 6.6 seconds.
- After those targeted repairs: 29 runnable files pass. Five files remain host-limited by the unchanged storage ancestor permission guard: `agent-port.postgres.test.ts` (one archive case), `backup.test.ts`, `git-backup-secrets.postgres.test.ts` (two cases), `git-backup.postgres.test.ts` (repository setup), and `update-preflight.conformance.test.ts` (baseline capture). The same ancestor is group-writable; no permission checks, baselines, or assertions were relaxed.

The PostgreSQL commands were `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/test-database-conformance.mjs --engine postgres --connection <disposable-dsn> -- <selected test files> --maxWorkers=1`. The final focused repair command selected `port-command.mixed.integration.test.ts` and `port-command-refusals.postgres.test.ts`: 2 files and 6 tests passed, 377.6 seconds wall including 65.8 seconds of shared worker compilation.

<details>
<summary>Existing slow consumer proof</summary>

The tooling pair passed 636 tests in 331.5 seconds (97% test time), dominated by its existing shell/Node fixture matrix. Whole-archive restore cases passed in 93.0, 42.8, and 48.7 seconds, including real store recovery and cold Gateway startup. Matrix account-root cases passed in 193.8, 174.8, and 69.8 seconds. The native port-command recovery cases range up to 114.4 seconds and deliberately exercise multiple full port/snapshot phases. Credential continuity cases reach 81.0 seconds; retained-agent update recovery took 81.1 seconds. These are existing broad compositions, not new planner-statistics work. The bounded mixed-suite worker-startup repair is described above; the dedicated one-shot custody proof remains intact.

</details>

Live-proof commands used isolated `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`. The Node integration harness ran via `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs .artifacts/port-live.mts`; PostgreSQL was a disposable local `pgvector/pgvector:pg17` container, with the same `unaccent`, `pg_trgm`, and `vector` prerequisites as CI. No remote lease or operator Gateway was used.

Limitations: `pnpm openclaw database port --family agent --to postgres --json` stopped before executing the port because the source launcher could not verify offline runtime-artifact publication. The live owner integration above succeeded instead; no service was stopped or guard bypassed. Existing archive and snapshot tests reject the group-writable storage-volume ancestor; filesystem permissions were left unchanged. Full `check:changed` SQLite inventory was skipped under the campaign's local gate budget; PR CI remains the broad proof.

Diff: production +146/-13 lines; tests +125/-3; docs +6/-0. No release changelog edit.
